artists.biography:
Alabama 3 are an English band mixing rock, dance, blues, country, gospel, and spoken word styles, founded in Brixton, London in 1995. In the United States, the band are known as A3, allegedly to avoid any possible legal conflict with the country music band Alabama. The group achieved international fame when the producers of hit TV series The Sopranos chose the track "Woke Up This Morning" for the show's opening credits.

The band are particularly notable for their fusion of styles, lyrics full of ironic intent, their deliberately humorous personas and their outrageous live performances. Every member of the group has an alias by which he is known, the band's founding members adopting the personas Larry Love (Rob Spragg) and The Very Reverend Dr. D. Wayne Love (Jake Black).

perplexity.description:
Exile on Coldharbour Lane is the debut album by Alabama 3, released on November 11, 1997, on One Little Indian and Geffen. The album's title and artwork reference The Rolling Stones' Exile on Main St., while also invoking Coldharbour Lane, a street in Brixton, South London known for its after-hours clubs and underground culture. This dual reference establishes the album's aesthetic: a fusion of classic rock lineage with contemporary urban grit. Recorded between March and June 1997, the album blends electronic production with blues and folk elements, creating a distinctive sound that draws from both traditional American roots music and modern dance and electronic influences.

The album features Alabama 3's distinctive vocal approach, with multiple singers including Larry Love and The Very Reverend Dr. D. Wayne Love contributing to the group's theatrical presentation. The production incorporates extensive sampling from blues and gospel sources, including material from Howlin' Wolf, Muddy Waters, and Mississippi Fred McDowell, grounding the electronic soundscapes in deep musical history. The album achieved limited commercial success in the United States, failing to chart on major album charts, though it gained significant cultural visibility through its most recognizable track, "Woke Up This Morning," which became the iconic opening theme for the television series The Sopranos.

Despite its modest chart performance, Exile on Coldharbour Lane established Alabama 3's artistic identity as genre-defying experimentalists willing to merge electronic production with blues and folk traditions. The album's influence extended beyond its initial release, with "Woke Up This Morning" becoming one of the most recognizable television themes of the era and later being sampled by hip-hop artist Nas. The album remains a notable entry in 1990s alternative music, representing a particular moment when electronic music and traditional American roots music intersected in innovative ways.
